results.notes:
Source is the saved 19-page NBER Summer Institute author manuscript: PDF pp. 3-4, 12-13 and 18-19, with the entire markdown conversion read. The OSF deposit named on PDF p. 11 is osf-xd7qw. All seven inspected data files match their manifest SHA-256 hashes. The older osf-q3gdu files contain 769 survey rows and 3774 grading rows, versus 786 and 4092 in osf-xd7qw; they are not combined. Participant exclusions follow 2 - clean.do, lines 28-174: completion/consent, earliest response per participant, six explicitly listed IDs, Excel quality checks (3 recoded to 1), and having graded before doing the task survey. Row counts after these successive stages are 786, 523, 505, 499, 457, 453. Grading follows the corrected 3 - grade cleaning_jul21.do specified in the July 21 ReadMe: exclude the tester, retry submissions, graders who previously completed the task survey, missing overall grades, and graders whose own-score regression on other evaluators' scores has slope below 0.1. This excludes 23 of 118 evaluators with human-essay pairs. All possible orderings of repeated same-grader pairs yield the same exclusion decisions. The authors retain repeated grading-session records; this analysis does likewise.

4 - main text figures.do, lines 556-588, establishes that Figure 1D uses the overall grade, not an average of overall, writing, content and originality. Keep linear and convex incentive arms, join cleaned long ratings to the cleaned participant sample, and select essay B when a_first=1 and essay A when a_first=0. The printed means are rating-weighted: 462 treatment and 501 control ratings. The paper does not print Figure 1 analysis participant counts; the new counts are 167 treatment and 186 control. The reproduced Table 1 counts and baseline means verify the cleaning pipeline but refer to all three incentive arms, not the Figure 1 sample.

Figure 1B separately uses the authors' wide participant-evaluator dataset: regress post-minus-pre overall grade on treatment, grader fixed effects, occupation-by-task-order fixed effects and incentive fixed effects, with participant-clustered SEs. This uses 1000 records from 352 people (166 treatment, 186 control); raw coefficient=0.698067260482, clustered SE=0.153804202732, and pre-treatment rating SD=1.70404045662. As in code lines 155-172 and 298-300, round the raw coefficient/SE to 0.001, divide by the pre-treatment rating SD, round to 0.01, and form/round the displayed interval using 1.96. This reproduces 0.41 and [0.23, 0.59]. These are replication checks, not the new participant-level effect or SE.

Computed fields use the Figure 1D post-treatment sample, averaging all retained overall ratings within each person before taking equally weighted arm means and sample SDs (ddof=1). Difference is the raw post-treatment treatment-minus-control mean difference on the 1-7 scale. Its SE is from OLS of this participant mean on an intercept and treatment indicator with HC2; independently checked against sqrt(s_treatment^2/n_treatment + s_control^2/n_control). Individual randomization justifies HC2 and n_clusters=null. The first task is a common baseline, not a randomized alternate AI condition; there is no paired crossover or first_round contrast. round=all denotes the sole post-intervention between-person comparison.
